claimCeiling: Registry inclusion means that a release illustrates a reusable method. It does not establish the release's correctness, novelty, independent reproduction or real-world impact.

methods.name: Certificate-first, proof-carrying research
methods.definition: Separate expensive discovery from cheaper checking by emitting a compact witness, proof object, bound or certificate with a fail-closed verifier.
methods.mechanism: Enables parallel candidate generation, reproducible rejection and bounded review without requiring every checker to repeat the discovery process.
failureModes: the substantive claim is translated incorrectly into the encoded proposition
generator and verifier share a defect
finite evidence is promoted to a universal theorem
certificate checking is described as independent reproduction

methods.name: Structural compression
methods.definition: Replace a high-dimensional search, state space or family of calculations with a lower-dimensional coordinate, invariant, kernel, normal form or representation.
methods.mechanism: Reduces search and verification cost by exposing the load-bearing structure instead of enumerating the original object space.
failureModes: the reduction faithfully solves the wrong formal object
a conditional analytic or semantic bridge is omitted
the reduced coordinate excludes relevant cases
bounded computation is mistaken for structural closure

methods.name: Exact regime stitching
methods.definition: Partition a large or infinite domain into explicitly covered regimes and use the most suitable exact method in each, with checked seams and endpoints.
methods.mechanism: Avoids forcing one monolithic method across scales while retaining a complete coverage argument.
failureModes: an endpoint or transition region is uncovered
normalisations differ across regimes
an external tail theorem is misapplied
the coverage checker shares the construction error

methods.name: Adversarial scientific controls
methods.definition: Deliberately corrupt signs, witnesses, manifests, assumptions or encodings and require the relevant validator to reject them.
methods.mechanism: Detects ceremonial replay, fail-open checks and fragile evidence pipelines before downstream work accumulates around them.
failureModes: only anticipated error classes are tested
producer-designed mutations share the producer specification
multiple internal routes are called independent
a green control suite is promoted to theorem verification

methods.name: Explicit research-lineage reuse
methods.definition: Publish parent-child dependencies and reusable components so an adjacent result can inherit a bounded object without reconstructing the entire programme.
methods.mechanism: Lowers reconstruction cost and makes cumulative method development inspectable.
failureModes: a child is misdescribed as independent confirmation
a common parent defect propagates across a lineage
dependencies are described only in prose
publication fragments work without standalone utility

methods.name: Productive failure and stop receipts
methods.definition: Retain failed routes and blockers, publish independently useful modules, and state precisely why the parent target remains open or the programme stopped.
methods.mechanism: Converts sunk work into reusable negative knowledge and can prevent repeated dead ends or unjustified continuation.
failureModes: selective disclosure hides unflattering failures
a trivial failure is published without decision value
a bounded calculation is inflated into the missing theorem
the unresolved parent target is obscured

methods.name: Identification before estimation
methods.definition: Specify the estimand, observation map, accounting identities and rival mechanisms, then test whether the available evidence can distinguish the target before estimating it.
methods.mechanism: Prevents false precision and redirects effort toward discriminating measurements or bounded conclusions.
failureModes: the rival class is too narrow
the observation map is semantically wrong
conditional non-identification is advertised as universal
non-identification is interpreted as a zero effect

methods.name: Partial identification and robust decisions
methods.definition: Characterise the admissible set and its sharp extrema, report incompatibility where appropriate, and identify decisions robust across the supported set.
methods.mechanism: Replaces unsupported point estimates and finite random clouds with bounded decision-relevant uncertainty.
failureModes: input uncertainty is frozen without disclosure
plausible states are excluded
sampled extrema are called sharp
utilities, rights or information costs are omitted

methods.name: Counterexample- and proxy-first analysis
methods.definition: Try to refute the proposed conjecture, proxy or search region before optimising or generalising it, and compare surrogates with the terminal outcome that matters.
methods.mechanism: Prunes invalid programmes early and exposes metric reversals, obstructions and approximation gaps.
failureModes: the target outcome is undefined
a narrow counterexample is overgeneralised
distributional relevance is untested
the invalidated proxy remains the decision criterion

methods.name: Certified decision margins
methods.definition: Compute how far inputs may move before a decision changes, or certify a result relative to a declared baseline with an explicit fallback when the sign is unresolved.
methods.mechanism: Concentrates recomputation and human attention near decision boundaries while preserving a safe incumbent elsewhere.
failureModes: the baseline is mismatched
switching or measurement costs are omitted
the model is transferred beyond its declared scope
nominal stability is confused with field robustness

methods.name: Assurance as a vector
methods.definition: Keep semantic mapping, certificate checking, producer replay, independent rerun, independent reimplementation, formal verification, specialist review, peer review and impact as separate claims.
methods.mechanism: Prevents evidence from one dimension borrowing credibility from another and directs scarce review to the unresolved gate.
failureModes: one omnibus badge replaces scoped states
correlated agents are counted as independent
producer replay is described as acceptance
protocol conformance is treated as impact

methods.name: Agent-readable research objects
methods.definition: Publish claims, dependencies, evidence, objections, open problems and replay routes in durable machine-readable forms alongside human explanations.
methods.mechanism: Reduces rediscovery and reconstruction cost when another person or agent audits, extends or challenges the work.
failureModes: machine-readable errors propagate faster
metadata integrity is confused with scientific truth
schemas omit the semantic boundary
communication assets are counted as evidence

methods.name: Staged adoption and impact evaluation
methods.definition: Keep method conformance separate from benefit and progress through usability, feasibility, controlled comparison and organisational follow-up with explicit stop rules.
methods.mechanism: Prevents model-only or structural checks from becoming workplace-impact claims and preserves evidence about burden, errors, rework and adoption.
failureModes: an underpowered pilot is promoted
missing outcomes are deleted
field association is called causal
average gain conceals harm or support cost

methodClusters.name: Binary-form Jacobian, determinant and obstruction toolkit
methodClusters.sharedBoundary: Related internal releases can reuse identities and methods but do not independently validate their shared mathematical or semantic premises.

methodClusters.name: Cyclicity and spectral compression
methodClusters.sharedBoundary: Exact algebraic or representation-theoretic compression does not discharge every analytic bridge or establish application-level impact.

methodClusters.name: Exact combinatorial certificate architecture
methodClusters.sharedBoundary: Certificate replay establishes encoded bounded claims; source-to-encoding correctness and independent reconstruction remain separate.

methodClusters.name: Identification and robust operations
methodClusters.sharedBoundary: Identified sets, exact bounds and decision margins are conditional on the declared observation map and model; real-world decision effects are unmeasured.

methodClusters.name: Sampling and optimisation diagnostics
methodClusters.sharedBoundary: Exact quadratic or finite-factor counterexamples do not establish frequency or magnitude in model-scale nonlinear workloads.

methodClusters.name: Grand-problem salvage
methodClusters.sharedBoundary: The extracted modules may be useful while the parent conjecture remains explicitly unresolved.

methodClusters.name: Cross-field identification and selector provenance
methodClusters.sharedBoundary: A common Selector Ledger can expose assumption-supported narrowing across fields without establishing that their observation maps share one exact symmetry, that the field mappings are independently validated, or that the reporting instrument improves practice.

methodClusters.name: Certified demographic identifiability auditing
methodClusters.sharedBoundary: Certified identified-set bounds and pre-registered audits expose what declared error models concede without establishing that any declared model is scientifically correct, that the underlying spectra are artefact-free, or that a setting-conditional verdict settles the biological dispute.

methodClusters.name: Wales policy-attribution identification audit
methodClusters.sharedBoundary: The constructive witness establishes non-identification only for the registered aggregate corpus, affected-road estimand and admitted rival class; it does not estimate the policy effect, settle policy merit or establish workflow impact.

methodClusters.name: Polydegree smooth-point and Fourier-persistence certificates
methodClusters.sharedBoundary: The all-degree conclusion depends jointly on the stated Jacobian smooth-point reduction, asymptotic Fourier limit, exact eventual envelope and finite Arb bridge. Producer-side replay and reuse of the earlier smooth-point package do not constitute independent theorem reconstruction, specialist review or evidence for the conjectural fixed-e programme.

methodClusters.name: Effective e=4 Polydegree persistence and scoped companion assurance

methodClusters.name: Aggregation licences and target sufficiency
methodClusters.sharedBoundary: A common fibre-factorisation diagnostic can expose missing decision-relevant information across fields without establishing that their scientific mechanisms are identical, that the admissible sets and targets are empirically valid, or that the proposed reporting licence improves research or policy decisions.

methodClusters.name: Frankl entropy obstruction and repaired reductions
methodClusters.sharedBoundary: The source-specific counterdirection and repaired support reductions do not prove the global candidate inequality, establish a new Frankl bound, validate the uninspected CISS text, or convert producer-side exact and directed-rounding checks into independent mathematical review.

methodClusters.name: Finite polynomial-rigidity certificates and executable frontier

lineages.name: Binary-form factorisation programme
lineages.basis: Each member explicitly identifies another member as foundational, parent, child, companion or continuation work in the published release metadata.
lineages.sharedBoundary: Dependency and reuse within this programme are not independent confirmation; a shared semantic or mathematical defect can propagate across the lineage.

lineages.name: Fixed-seed cyclicity programme
lineages.basis: The root-span release explicitly cites the cyclicity-loci release as its predecessor and extends the same fixed-seed cyclicity programme.
lineages.sharedBoundary: The child release reuses the fixed-seed framework and therefore does not independently confirm the parent release or its analytic bridge.

lineages.name: Affine diversification partial-identification programme
lineages.basis: The finite-sample successor explicitly extends the predecessor's affine cumulative-loss fibre, fixed-signal sharp bounds and endpoint-sampling diagnostic by adding signal uncertainty, three-valued decisions and a frozen CRABS comparison.
lineages.sharedBoundary: The successor reuses the predecessor's mathematical and software framework and therefore does not independently confirm it. A shared error in the affine coordinate, probability bridge or encoding can propagate across the lineage.

lineages.name: Exact joint-replenishment certification programme
lineages.basis: The three-item successor explicitly extends the parent's common-origin model, independent-cap reduction boundary, exact two-item interval and certificate-first conventions with a distinct primitive-triple tail architecture and logistics evaluation handoff.
lineages.sharedBoundary: The successor reuses parent assumptions, code patterns and producer coordination. This lineage is dependency evidence, not independent confirmation, and a shared semantic, algebraic or implementation defect may propagate across both releases.

lineages.name: TxGraffiti cubic-counterexample order programme
lineages.basis: The order-48 successor explicitly identifies the public 50-vertex release as its parent, supplies a different smaller graph and resolves the parent's open below-50 search direction by construction without retracting the parent or inheriting its separate restricted-class theorems.
lineages.sharedBoundary: The successor reuses problem framing, provenance and certificate architecture from the parent. This lineage is dependency evidence, not independent confirmation, and a shared source-to-semantics or implementation defect may propagate across both releases.

rules: Do not rewrite a published method, method cluster, lineage identity, name, basis, root or shared boundary, or release assignment in place; retain the prior entry and use a new identifier or dated successor for a semantic replacement.

Append a lineage member only at the tail after its release declares the reciprocal lineage identifier and an evidential parent link to an earlier member, unless it is the explicitly registered root; never delete, replace or reorder a published member.
Append a dated changeLog entry for every semantic addition, correction, deprecation or reassignment.
Keep broad method clustering separate from evidence-backed research lineage, and do not infer lineage from topical similarity alone.
Registry inclusion or revision does not promote correctness, novelty, independent reproduction or real-world impact.
